body.x: As a participant in the K-Startup Joint Pavilion, Eureka Park, the area dedicated for startups during CES 2023, which was held in Las Vegas, U.S. for four days from Thursday, January 5 to Sunday, January 8 in local time, Moverse (CEO Yong-Jun Hyung) presented its 3D metaverse choreography creation solution.

The business has developed and supplied 3D motions certified by creators to the digital markets that are widely known within the metaverse and among virtual human beings. Thanks to this experience, the firm has made agreements with game developers and metaverse platforms, and recently established a U.S. branch, intensifying their efforts to target the domestic and overseas markets with dance motions that are freed from copyright issues.

At CES 2023, Moverse introduced a self-directed choreography creation solution by combining short pieces of choreography. This is a technology for producing content for social media using 3D metaverse graphics. Currently, users are allowed to create their own avatars and use them to edit and produce various choreographic videos on this platform that is now available for free via the official website of Moverse.

There are two options to be applied to each avatar: the user's real face converted into a 3D graphic or a general style 3D model. In addition, K-pop choreography moves and various background music, images, and videos produced by Moverse can be inserted into videos, along with different items provided on a partially charged service.

There are various interesting options for the resulting videos to be published on social media to express the user’s personalities or celebrate certain anniversaries. Moverse also emphasized the ease-of-use and that making videos is as simple as making PowerPoint slides.

body.x: According to Yong-Jun Hyung, CEO of Moverse, “Our platform’s primary targets are influencers who wish to create and use 3D avatars for the metaverse. We have recently achieved significant results by signing B2B platform supply contracts with global metaverse platforms from Israel and France.” CEO Hyung added that “At this year's CES, we'd like to find large-sized customers like Facebook's parent company, Meta, that can cooperate with us in supplying content. To this end, we have completed various choreography motions, and additional motions are currently under development.”

“As China's TikTok gained a unique position in the global social media market with its dance music and choreography videos, we aim to establish ourselves as a 3D avatar-based social media platform in the future,” CEO Hyung explained. “In order to realize that goal, we are committed to continuously offering new services.”

Meanwhile, CES, the world's largest IT fair, is an exhibition that provides a comprehensive look of the global consumer electronics industry in just one place. It is held annually in Las Vegas in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). Aving News has annually reported on CES news for the world for 17 consecutive years since 2006, hosting the Best of CES which selects the best innovative products and technologies, and the Best of Made in Korea that chooses the most innovative businesses in South Korea. In addition, the media has delivered breaking news about CES through AVING LIVE.

The K-Startup Joint Pavilion is jointly attended by Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation while 51 Korean innovators participate to tap into the U.S. market and discover global partners. In addition, CES 2023 university student supporters selected from Kyung Hee, Kookmin, Sogang, and Chung-Ang Universities are matched based on their specialties and the participating businesses' industry fields.
